background_need: Fictional community arts groups across two neighboring regions report limited capacity to choose, test, and maintain basic digital tools. The idea is to build practical confidence through short peer-supported activities.

objectives.description: Improve participants' ability to select and use a digital tool for a routine organizational task.
Help participating groups establish a realistic plan for continuing one new digital practice.

target_groups: Staff and volunteers at fictional community arts groups

preliminary_activities.description: Run a short introductory workshop using fictional organizational scenarios.
Facilitate a peer lab where participants try selected tools and discuss accessibility.
Support each group to outline a small follow-up practice and review date.

expected_results.description: Participants demonstrate one practical digital task in a workshop or peer-lab exercise.
Participating groups produce a brief plan to continue one selected digital practice.

proposed_indicators.description: Number of participants who complete a practical digital task to an agreed checklist.
proposed_indicators.measurement_method: Count completed checklists at the end of the fictional workshop exercises.

proposed_indicators.description: Number of participating groups with a written follow-up practice plan.
proposed_indicators.measurement_method: Count plans reviewed against a short completeness checklist.

assumptions: Participating groups can set aside time for short learning activities.
open_questions: Which digital tasks are most relevant to the participating groups?
What lightweight follow-up support would be practical?
